{{Quote|You will have a more pleasant death at our hands than the malia. Our poisons are quick.|A Ragoon hunter to Qui-Gon Jinn|<ref name="Ties" />}}
The '''Ragoons''' were the native [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ragoon VI]]. A short species with brown, leathery skin, they had long and pointed [[Ear/Legends|ears]]. Ragoon society was pre-industrial, as the species preferred to keep the environment of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] pristine and free from exploitation. In order to achieve that, they forbade colonization of Ragoon VI, and, when their numbers dwindled through sickness, entrusted their planet to the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] for safekeeping. Offworld visitors were then restricted, although members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and the inhabitants of the neighboring planet [[Aaeton]] were allowed to visit more frequently. The [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] encountered a group of Ragoons during a [[Jedi training/Legends|training]] mission to the world.

==Biology and appearance==
The Ragoons were a short [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. They had brown, leathery skin, and their heads were covered in thick [[Hair/Legends|hair]]. They had long, pointed [[Ear/Legends|ears]] and a powerfully built physique.<ref name="Ties" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|This is beautiful country, but a hard one. I know the tribes use the malia for the food and skins they provide. They are hard to kill, and very valuable. That was their main concern. Most beings in the galaxy do not kill without purpose. If you can discover what that purpose is, you can forestall a battle.|Qui-Gon Jinn|<ref name="Ties" />}}
The Ragoons intentionally resisted the development of [[City/Legends|cities]] and advanced industry.<ref name="Ties" /> They valued the unsoiled environment of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], and maintaining that became their first priority.<ref name="Trail">''[[Jedi Quest: The Trail of the Jedi]]''</ref> The Ragoons were organized into tribes<ref name="Ties" /> and had a government with which they had contact with the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]].<ref name="Trail" /> Individual Ragoons were able to speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]].<ref name="Ties" />

The Ragoons used long tubes of polished stone as [[Blowgun/Legends|blowpipes]] to shoot [[Poison/Legends|poison]]-tipped [[Dart/Legends|darts]], which they used to [[Hunting/Legends|hunt]] a local predator known as the [[Malia/Legends|malia]]. Those animals hunted in a pack and were extremely quick, with long, sharp [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]], but they provided the Ragoons with meat as well as skins that could be used for a variety of purposes.<ref name="Ties" />

==History==
[[File:Obiwanquinlan.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Obi-Wan Kenobi and Quinlan Vos on Ragoon VI during a training mission in 44 BBY.]]
{{Quote|The Ragoons never allowed colonizers to settle. Their own population sickened and dwindled until finally there was only a handful left. They could no longer keep out all those who wanted to come. They knew they would have to give up what they loved most in order to save it.|Wren Honoran|<ref name="Trail" />}}
The Ragoons were native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ragoon VI]],<ref name="Ties" /> located within [[The Negs]] section of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]],<ref name="The Essential Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> and known for its spectacular and remote beauty.<ref name="Ties" /> They never allowed colonization of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], preferring to keep Ragoon VI in pristine condition.<ref name="Trail" /> They had no cities on their planet and lacked any industry to give off emissions into the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]], but they encountered offworlders who visited the planet.<ref name="Ties" /> However, during the administration of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], large numbers of Ragoons sickened, and their population decreased. Aware that they could no longer protect the integrity of their world by their own means, the Ragoon government gave control of the planet to the Galactic Senate on trust, to ensure it remained unspoiled. A Senate committee then gave permits to small groups of individuals to visit the planet<ref name="Trail" /> and allowed special access to the natives of [[Aaeton]], a neighboring planet that provided refuge to Ragoon elders,<ref name="Trail" /> as well as to members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] for [[Jedi training/Legends|training]] purposes.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|III|74|Ragoon 6}}</ref> Numerous [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], such as [[Tahl]], [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]],<ref name="Ties" /> [[Wren Honoran]], [[Winso Bykart]],<ref name="Trail" /> and [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]], subsequently visited the world.<ref name="Star Wars: Republic: Dreadnaughts of Rendili">''[[Star Wars: Republic: Dreadnaughts of Rendili]]''</ref>

In [[41 BBY/Legends|41 BBY]], during a harsh winter, a group of Ragoons encountered Jinn and his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], Kenobi, during a Jedi training mission. The pair of Jedi were encircled by a pack of malia; and despite having [[Death/Legends|killed]] one of the creatures, they were still in danger when the Ragoons arrived. Killing a second malia with their blowpipes, the Ragoons threatened to kill the Jedi. Jinn, who had traveled to the planet before, recognized that the first priority of the Ragoons was to obtain the malia meat. He offered them the carcass, the two groups parted in peace, and the Jedi left the planet shortly thereafter.<ref name="Ties" /> Kenobi later returned to the planet in [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]], this time accompanied by his own Padawan, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]].<ref name="Trail" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Ragoons first appeared, albiet unidentified, in ''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Ties That Bind]]'', a [[2001]] young-adult novel by [[Jude Watson]].<ref name="Ties" /> They were first identified in the [[2002]] young-adult novel ''[[Jedi Quest: The Trail of the Jedi]]'', also written by Watson.<ref name="Trail" />
